passages.text: Then Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had gone there to make him king.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was the son of Solomon.
Rehoboam became king after Solomon died.
Rehoboam went to Shechem.
All Israel had gone to Shechem.
The people of Israel went there to make Rehoboam king.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֖ם שְׁכֶ֑ם כִּ֥י שְׁכֶ֛ם בָּ֥א כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְהַמְלִ֥יךְ אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about this, he was still in Egypt where he had fled from King Solomon and had been living ever since.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the son of Nebat.
Jeroboam was living in Egypt.
Jeroboam had fled to Egypt.
He fled from King Solomon.
Jeroboam remained in Egypt.
Jeroboam heard the news while he was still in Egypt.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ׀ יָרָבְעָ֣ם בֶּן־ נְבָ֗ט וְהוּא֙ עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ בְמִצְרַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּרַ֔ח מִפְּנֵ֖י הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב יָרָבְעָ֖ם בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: So they sent for Jeroboam, and he and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said, “Your father put a heavy yoke on us. But now you should lighten the burden of your father’s service and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you.”
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the son of Nebat.
He was living in Egypt.
The people of Israel sent for Jeroboam.
Jeroboam came with the whole assembly of Israel.
They all came to Rehoboam.
They spoke to Rehoboam.
They said, “Your father made our yoke heavy.
Now lighten the hard service of your father.
Lighten the heavy yoke he put on us.
If you do this, we will serve you.”
passages.original: וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ וַיִּקְרְאוּ־ ל֔וֹ וַיָּבֹאוּ יָרָבְעָ֖ם וְכָל־ קְהַ֣ל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיְדַבְּר֔וּ אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ אָבִ֖יךָ הִקְשָׁ֣ה אֶת־ עֻלֵּ֑נוּ וְאַתָּ֡ה עַתָּ֣ה הָקֵל֩ מֵעֲבֹדַ֨ת אָבִ֜יךָ הַקָּשָׁ֗ה וּמֵעֻלּ֧וֹ הַכָּבֵ֛ד אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥ן עָלֵ֖ינוּ וְנַעַבְדֶֽךָּ׃

passages.text: Rehoboam answered, “Go away for three days and then return to me.” So the people departed.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was the king of Israel at this time.
Rehoboam spoke to the people.
He said, "Go away for three days."
He said, "Then return to me."
The people left.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם לְכ֥וּ עֹ֛ד שְׁלֹשָׁ֥ה יָמִ֖ים וְשׁ֣וּבוּ אֵלָ֑י וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ הָעָֽם׃

passages.text: Then King Rehoboam consulted with the elders who had served his father Solomon during his lifetime. “How do you advise me to respond to these people?” he asked.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam was the son of Solomon.
Solomon had been king before Rehoboam.
Solomon had wise elders who served him while he was alive.
Rehoboam became king after Solomon died.
Rehoboam called the elders who had served his father.
Rehoboam spoke to these elders.
He asked them for advice.
He said, “How do you advise me to answer these people?”
passages.original: וַיִּוָּעַ֞ץ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת־ הַזְּקֵנִים֙ אֲשֶׁר־ הָי֣וּ עֹמְדִ֗ים אֶת־ פְּנֵי֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה אָבִ֔יו בִּֽהְיֹת֥וֹ חַ֖י לֵאמֹ֑ר אֵ֚יךְ אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת־ הָֽעָם־ הַזֶּ֖ה דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: They replied, “If you will be a servant to these people and serve them this day, and if you will respond by speaking kind words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
passages.sermon:
The elders spoke to King Rehoboam.
They said, "Be a servant to these people today.
Serve them.
Answer them.
Speak kind words to them.
If you do this, they will serve you always."
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּר אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר אִם־ הַ֠יּוֹם תִּֽהְיֶה־ עֶ֜בֶד לָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וַֽעֲבַדְתָּ֔ם וַעֲנִיתָ֕ם וְדִבַּרְתָּ֥ אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם דְּבָרִ֣ים טוֹבִ֑ים וְהָי֥וּ לְךָ֛ עֲבָדִ֖ים כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: But Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders; instead, he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served him.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam was the son of Solomon.
Rehoboam received advice from the elders who had served his father Solomon.
Rehoboam rejected the advice of these elders.
Rehoboam chose not to follow their counsel.
Rehoboam then consulted the young men.
These young men had grown up with Rehoboam.
These young men served Rehoboam and stood before him.
passages.original: וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת־ עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְעָצֻ֑הוּ וַיִּוָּעַ֗ץ אֶת־ הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָעֹמְדִ֖ים לְפָנָֽיו׃

passages.text: He asked them, “What message do you advise that we send back to these people who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was the king of Israel.
He spoke to the young men who had grown up with him.
He asked them a question.
He said, “What advice do you give me?”
He wanted to know what message to send to the people.
The people had come to him with a request.
They said, “Your father put a heavy yoke on us.”
They asked him to make their burden lighter.
Rehoboam asked the young men how he should answer the people.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם מָ֚ה אַתֶּ֣ם נֽוֹעָצִ֔ים וְנָשִׁ֥יב דָּבָ֖ר אֶת־ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבְּר֤וּ אֵלַי֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הָקֵל֙ מִן־ הָעֹ֔ל אֲשֶׁר־ נָתַ֥ן אָבִ֖יךָ עָלֵֽינוּ׃

passages.text: The young men who had grown up with him replied, “This is how you should answer these people who said to you, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you should make it lighter.’ This is what you should tell them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist!
passages.sermon:
The young men had grown up with Rehoboam.
They replied to him.
They said, "This is how you should answer these people."
These people said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy.'
They also said, 'You should make it lighter.'
You should say to them, 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.'
passages.original: וַיְדַבְּר֣וּ אֵלָ֗יו הַיְלָדִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר גָּדְל֣וּ אִתּוֹ֮ לֵאמֹר֒ כֹּֽה־ תֹאמַ֣ר לָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֡ה אֲשֶׁר֩ דִּבְּר֨וּ אֵלֶ֜יךָ לֵאמֹ֗ר אָבִ֙יךָ֙ הִכְבִּ֣יד אֶת־ עֻלֵּ֔נוּ וְאַתָּ֖ה הָקֵ֣ל מֵעָלֵ֑ינוּ כֹּ֚ה תְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם קָֽטָנִּ֥י עָבָ֖ה מִמָּתְנֵ֥י אָבִֽי׃

passages.text: Whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.’ ”
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam spoke to the people of Israel.
He said his father, King Solomon, gave them a heavy burden.
He said, "My father put a heavy yoke on you."
He said, "I will make your yoke even heavier."
He said, "My father punished you with whips."
He said, "I will punish you with scorpions."
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה אָבִי֙ הֶעְמִ֤יס עֲלֵיכֶם֙ עֹ֣ל כָּבֵ֔ד וַאֲנִ֖י אוֹסִ֣יף עַֽל־ עֻלְּכֶ֑ם אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֕י אֲיַסֵּ֥ר אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעַקְרַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: After three days, Jeroboam and all the people returned to Rehoboam, since the king had said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was a leader among the people of Israel.
Rehoboam was the king of Israel at that time.
Three days passed.
Jeroboam and all the people came back to Rehoboam.
The king had told them to return after three days.
He said, “Come back to me on the third day.”
passages.original: וַיָּבוֹ יָרָבְעָ֧ם וְכָל־ הָעָ֛ם אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֖ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר שׁ֥וּבוּ אֵלַ֖י בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִֽׁי׃

passages.text: And the king answered the people harshly. He rejected the advice of the elders and spoke to them as the young men had advised, saying, “Whereas my father made your yoke heavy, I will add to your yoke. Whereas my father scourged you with whips, I will scourge you with scorpions.”
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam spoke to the people.
He answered them harshly.
He rejected the advice of the elders.
He chose to follow the advice of the young men.
He said, “My father made your yoke heavy.
I will add to your yoke.
My father punished you with whips.
I will punish you with scorpions.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֧עַן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ אֶת־ הָעָ֖ם קָשָׁ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲזֹ֛ב אֶת־ עֲצַ֥ת הַזְּקֵנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְעָצֻֽהוּ׃ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם כַּעֲצַ֤ת הַיְלָדִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אָבִי֙ הִכְבִּ֣יד אֶֽת־ עֻלְּכֶ֔ם וַאֲנִ֖י אֹסִ֣יף עַֽל־ עֻלְּכֶ֑ם אָבִ֗י יִסַּ֤ר אֶתְכֶם֙ בַּשּׁוֹטִ֔ים וַאֲנִ֕י אֲיַסֵּ֥ר אֶתְכֶ֖ם בָּעַקְרַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: So the king did not listen to the people, and indeed this turn of events was from the LORD, to fulfill the word He had spoken to Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah the Shilonite.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam did not listen to the people.
This happened because the LORD caused it.
The LORD wanted to fulfill His word.
The LORD had spoken this word to Jeroboam son of Nebat.
The LORD spoke through Ahijah the Shilonite.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ שָׁמַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל־ הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי־ הָיְתָ֤ה סִבָּה֙ מֵעִ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה לְמַ֜עַן הָקִ֣ים אֶת־ דְּבָר֗וֹ אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ בְּיַד֙ אֲחִיָּ֣ה הַשִּׁילֹנִ֔י אֶל־ יָרָבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־ נְבָֽט׃

passages.text: When all Israel saw that the king had refused to listen to them, they answered the king: “What portion do we have in David, and what inheritance in the son of Jesse? To your tents, O Israel! Look now to your own house, O David!” So the Israelites went home, but Rehoboam still reigned over the Israelites living in the cities of Judah.
passages.sermon:
All Israel saw that King Rehoboam refused to listen to them.
The people of Israel spoke to the king.
They said, “We have no share in David.
We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse.
Go to your tents, Israel.
Now, David, look after your own house.”
The Israelites went home.
But the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah remained.
Rehoboam ruled over them.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣רְא כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כִּ֠י לֹֽא־ שָׁמַ֣ע הַמֶּלֶךְ֮ אֲלֵיהֶם֒ וַיָּשִׁ֣בוּ הָעָ֣ם אֶת־ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּבָ֣ר׀ לֵאמֹ֡ר מַה־ לָּנוּ֩ חֵ֨לֶק בְּדָוִ֜ד וְלֹֽא־ נַחֲלָ֣ה בְּבֶן־ יִשַׁ֗י לְאֹהָלֶ֙יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עַתָּ֕ה רְאֵ֥ה בֵיתְךָ֖ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃ וּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בְּעָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם רְחַבְעָֽם׃פ

passages.text: Then King Rehoboam sent out Adoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. And King Rehoboam mounted his chariot in haste and escaped to Jerusalem.
passages.sermon:
King Rehoboam ruled over Judah.
Adoram managed the forced labor for the king.
King Rehoboam sent Adoram to the people of Israel.
All Israel stoned Adoram with stones.
Adoram died from the stoning.
King Rehoboam acted quickly.
He got into his chariot.
He fled to Jerusalem.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם אֶת־ אֲדֹרָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־ הַמַּ֔ס וַיִּרְגְּמ֨וּ כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֥ל בּ֛וֹ אֶ֖בֶן וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ רְחַבְעָ֗ם הִתְאַמֵּץ֙ לַעֲל֣וֹת בַּמֶּרְכָּבָ֔ה לָנ֖וּס יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: So to this day Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David.
passages.sermon: Israel rebelled against the house of David.\r\nThis rebellion continued until today.
passages.original: וַיִּפְשְׁע֤וּ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ בְּבֵ֣ית דָּוִ֔ד עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they summoned him to the assembly and made him king over all Israel. Only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was a leader in Israel.
All Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned.
The people of Israel sent for Jeroboam.
They called Jeroboam to the assembly.
The people made Jeroboam king over all Israel.
The house of David ruled only the tribe of Judah.
No other tribe followed the house of David.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֞י כִּשְׁמֹ֤עַ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ כִּֽי־ שָׁ֣ב יָרָבְעָ֔ם וַֽיִּשְׁלְח֗וּ וַיִּקְרְא֤וּ אֹתוֹ֙ אֶל־ הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה וַיַּמְלִ֥יכוּ אֹת֖וֹ עַל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לֹ֤א הָיָה֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י בֵית־ דָּוִ֔ד זוּלָתִ֥י שֵֽׁבֶט־ יְהוּדָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: And when Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he mobilized the whole house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin—180,000 chosen warriors—to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
passages.sermon:
Rehoboam was the son of Solomon.
Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem.
He gathered all the men from the house of Judah.
He also gathered the tribe of Benjamin.
He chose 180,000 young warriors.
These men were ready for battle.
Rehoboam planned to fight against the house of Israel.
He wanted to bring the kingdom back to himself.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹאוּ רְחַבְעָם֮ יְרוּשָׁלִַם֒ וַיַּקְהֵל֩ אֶת־ כָּל־ בֵּ֨ית יְהוּדָ֜ה וְאֶת־ שֵׁ֣בֶט בִּנְיָמִ֗ן מֵאָ֨ה וּשְׁמֹנִ֥ים אֶ֛לֶף בָּח֖וּר עֹשֵׂ֣ה מִלְחָמָ֑ה לְהִלָּחֵם֙ עִם־ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לְהָשִׁיב֙ אֶת־ הַמְּלוּכָ֔ה לִרְחַבְעָ֖ם בֶּן־ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃פ

passages.text: But the word of God came to Shemaiah the man of God: “Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and the rest of the people that this is what the LORD says: ‘You are not to go up and fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Each of you must return home, for this word is from Me.’ ” So they listened to the word of the LORD and turned back according to the word of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Shemaiah.
Shemaiah was a man of God.
God gave Shemaiah a message.
God told Shemaiah to speak to Rehoboam.
Rehoboam was the son of Solomon.
Rehoboam was king of Judah.
God told Shemaiah to speak to all the house of Judah.
God told Shemaiah to speak to the tribe of Benjamin.
God told Shemaiah to speak to the rest of the people.
God said, “This is what the LORD says.
Do not go up to fight against your brothers.
Your brothers are the Israelites.
Each of you must return to his home.
This word comes from Me.”
The people listened to the word of the LORD.
They turned back.
They went away as the LORD had said.
passages.original: וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַ֣ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים אֶל־ שְׁמַעְיָ֥ה אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵאמֹֽר׃ אֱמֹ֗ר אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֤ם בֶּן־ שְׁלֹמֹה֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֶל־ כָּל־ בֵּ֥ית יְהוּדָ֖ה וּבִנְיָמִ֑ין וְיֶ֥תֶר הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃ כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֡ה לֹֽא־ תַעֲלוּ֩ וְלֹא־ תִלָּ֨חֲמ֜וּן עִם־ אֲחֵיכֶ֣ם בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל שׁ֚וּבוּ אִ֣ישׁ לְבֵית֔וֹ כִּ֧י מֵאִתִּ֛י נִהְיָ֖ה הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ אֶת־ דְּבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּשֻׁ֥בוּ לָלֶ֖כֶת כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Then Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. And from there he went out and built Penuel.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the king of Israel.
He built the city of Shechem.
Shechem was in the hill country of Ephraim.
Jeroboam lived in Shechem.
After that, Jeroboam left Shechem.
He built the city of Penuel.
passages.original: וַיִּ֨בֶן יָרָבְעָ֧ם אֶת־ שְׁכֶ֛ם בְּהַ֥ר אֶפְרַ֖יִם וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב בָּ֑הּ וַיֵּצֵ֣א מִשָּׁ֔ם וַיִּ֖בֶן אֶת־ פְּנוּאֵֽל׃

passages.text: Jeroboam said in his heart, “Now the kingdom might revert to the house of David.
passages.sermon: Jeroboam was the king of Israel.\r\nHe thought to himself.\r\nHe said in his heart, “Now the kingdom might return to the house of David.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יָרָבְעָ֖ם בְּלִבּ֑וֹ עַתָּ֛ה תָּשׁ֥וּב הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה לְבֵ֥ית דָּוִֽד׃

passages.text: If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the LORD at Jerusalem, their hearts will return to their lord, Rehoboam king of Judah; then they will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.”
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the king of Israel.
\r\nHe spoke about the people of Israel.
\r\nHe said, “If these people go up to Jerusalem,
\r\nThey will offer sacrifices at the house of the LORD.
\r\nThen the hearts of these people will turn back to their master.
\r\nTheir master is Rehoboam, the king of Judah.
\r\nThey will kill me.
\r\nAfter that, they will return to Rehoboam, the king of Judah.”
passages.original: אִֽם־ יַעֲלֶ֣ה׀ הָעָ֣ם הַזֶּ֗ה לַעֲשׂ֨וֹת זְבָחִ֤ים בְּבֵית־ יְהוָה֙ בִּיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וְ֠שָׁב לֵ֣ב הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ אֶל־ אֲדֹ֣נֵיהֶ֔ם אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֖ם מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַהֲרָגֻ֕נִי וְשָׁ֖בוּ אֶל־ רְחַבְעָ֥ם מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: After seeking advice, the king made two golden calves and said to the people, “Going up to Jerusalem is too much for you. Here, O Israel, are your gods, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.”
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the king of Israel.
Jeroboam wanted to keep his people from returning to Rehoboam, king of Judah.
Jeroboam sought advice.
Jeroboam made two golden calves.
Jeroboam spoke to the people of Israel.
Jeroboam said, "It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem."
Jeroboam said, "Here are your gods, O Israel."
Jeroboam said, "These gods brought you up out of the land of Egypt."
passages.original: וַיִּוָּעַ֣ץ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּ֕עַשׂ שְׁנֵ֖י עֶגְלֵ֣י זָהָ֑ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם רַב־ לָכֶם֙ מֵעֲל֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֔ם הִנֵּ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶעֱל֖וּךָ מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃

passages.text: One calf he set up in Bethel, and the other in Dan.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the king of Israel.
Jeroboam made two golden calves.
Jeroboam set up one golden calf in Bethel.
Jeroboam set up the other golden calf in Dan.
passages.original: וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת־ הָאֶחָ֖ד בְּבֵֽית־ אֵ֑ל וְאֶת־ הָאֶחָ֖ד נָתַ֥ן בְּדָֽן׃

passages.text: And this thing became a sin; the people walked as far as Dan to worship before one of the calves.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the king of Israel.
He made two golden calves for the people.
This act became a sin for Israel.
The people traveled to Dan.
They went there to worship before one of the golden calves.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֛י הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה לְחַטָּ֑את וַיֵּלְכ֥וּ הָעָ֛ם לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֶחָ֖ד עַד־ דָּֽן׃

passages.text: Jeroboam also built shrines on the high places and appointed from every class of people priests who were not Levites.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was king of Israel.
Jeroboam built shrines on the high places.
He chose priests from all the people.
These priests were not Levites.
passages.original: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אֶת־ בֵּ֣ית בָּמ֑וֹת וַיַּ֤עַשׂ כֹּֽהֲנִים֙ מִקְצ֣וֹת הָעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־ הָי֖וּ מִבְּנֵ֥י לֵוִֽי׃

passages.text: And Jeroboam ordained a feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the feast that was in Judah, and he offered sacrifices on the altar; he made this offering in Bethel to sacrifice to the calves he had set up, and he installed priests in Bethel for the high places he had set up.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was the king of Israel.
He created a feast.
He chose the fifteenth day of the eighth month for this feast.
This date was like the feast in Judah.
Jeroboam went up to the altar.
He offered sacrifices on the altar.
He did this in Bethel.
He sacrificed to the calves he had made.
Jeroboam set up priests in Bethel.
These priests served at the high places he had made.
passages.original: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ יָרָבְעָ֣ם׀ חָ֡ג בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִ֣י בַּחֲמִשָּֽׁה־ עָשָׂר֩ י֨וֹם׀ לַחֹ֜דֶשׁ כֶּחָ֣ג׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּיהוּדָ֗ה וַיַּ֙עַל֙ עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ כֵּ֤ן עָשָׂה֙ בְּבֵֽית־ אֵ֔ל לְזַבֵּ֖חַ לָעֲגָלִ֣ים אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֑ה וְהֶעֱמִיד֙ בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔ל אֶת־ כֹּהֲנֵ֥י הַבָּמ֖וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָֽׂה׃

passages.text: On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a month of his own choosing, Jeroboam offered sacrifices on the altar he had set up in Bethel. So he ordained a feast for the Israelites, offered sacrifices on the altar, and burned incense.
passages.sermon:
Jeroboam was king of Israel.
He set up an altar in Bethel.
He chose the eighth month for a special event.
He picked the fifteenth day of that month.
He invented this month by himself.
On that day, Jeroboam went up to the altar.
He offered sacrifices on the altar.
He made a feast for the people of Israel.
He burned incense on the altar.
passages.original: וַיַּ֜עַל עַֽל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֣חַ׀ אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֣ה בְּבֵֽית־ אֵ֗ל בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה עָשָׂ֥ר יוֹם֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁמִינִ֔י בַּחֹ֖דֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר־ בָּדָ֣א מִלִּבַּד וַיַּ֤עַשׂ חָג֙ לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיַּ֥עַל עַל־ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ לְהַקְטִֽיר׃פ
